title: Serbs
capsule: The dataset window 1805–1880 covers the emergence of autonomous and then fully independent Serbia from Ottoman rule. The First Serbian Uprising of 1804–1813, led by Karađorđe, and the Second Uprising of 1815, led by Miloš Obrenović, secured Serbian autonomy recognized by the Ottoman Porte in 1830. The Principality of Serbia progressively expanded its territory and reduced Ottoman suzerainty through the 1860s under Mihailo Obrenović III, who expelled Ottoman garrisons from Serbian fortresses in 1867; full independence was internationally recognized at the Congress of Berlin in 1878 and formalized in the Treaty of Constantinople in 1879, with the Kingdom of Serbia proclaimed in 1882.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. This entry covers the Serb ethnopolitical entity rather than a fixed state; territorial extent during 1805–1880 varied substantially and the mapping of Serbian-populated areas versus the Principality's recognized borders introduces ambiguity.
